title: Dynamic code execution via eval() — review required
description: A direct call to eval() executes a string as code. If any part of the string is attacker-influenced this is code injection; even with static strings, eval() defeats static analysis and Content-Security-Policy. This lexical rule cannot prove taint — treat every hit as review-required, not as proven exploitable.
remediation: Remove eval(): use JSON.parse for data, a function map or allowlisted dispatch for behavior, and URL/URLSearchParams for parsing. If eval() is unavoidable, never pass interpolated or concatenated input.
limitation: Lexical, line-based, no dataflow: matches any direct eval( call including safe static strings. new Function is out of scope for this rule.
